metadata.title: Drive reset after emergency stop
metadata.summary: Diagnose why an infeed conveyor does not restart after an emergency-stop release even though its run command remains active.

scenario.initial_context: An infeed conveyor was stopped by an emergency stop during packaging production. The emergency stop has been physically released, but the conveyor does not restart.
scenario.operational_state: The PLC run command is reported active, communication loss is not reported, and the motor remains stationary.
scenario.initiating_event: An emergency stop interrupted conveyor operation.
scenario.learner_role: Automation engineer responsible for evidence-based diagnosis and controlled recovery.

safety_context.safe_state: The machine must remain in a controlled non-moving state until the safety chain, drive permission, and restart conditions are verified.
intervention_constraints: Do not bypass or defeat any safety function.
Obtain authorization before issuing a reset or controlled movement command.
Preserve diagnostic evidence before applying a reset.
Keep personnel clear of hazardous movement during controlled testing.
Release the machine only after safety and functional validation.

stages.title: Stabilize the incident
stages.situation: The emergency stop has been released, the conveyor is stationary, and a run command is reported active.

decisions.action: Confirm the controlled safe state, physical emergency-stop release, applicable safety status, and authorization boundaries before diagnosis.
Attempt an immediate restart without confirming the safety chain or clearing the hazardous area.

stages.title: Separate command from execution
stages.situation: The machine is controlled and safe for non-invasive status inspection.

decisions.action: Correlate the PLC run command, HMI indication, and physical motor movement.
Repeat the start command before comparing command and movement states.

stages.title: Inspect drive operating state
stages.situation: The run command is confirmed active while the motor remains stationary.

decisions.action: Inspect communication health and the drive's generic operational permission and readiness states.
Prioritize a communication-loss investigation despite the absence of a reported communication fault.

stages.title: Test the recovery hypothesis
stages.situation: Communication is present, but the drive is not confirmed ready for controlled operation.

decisions.action: Compare the observed safety and drive states with the approved functional recovery procedure.
Try another controlled start, then review the recovery procedure when movement still does not occur.

stages.title: Perform an authorized reset
stages.situation: The available evidence supports an incomplete recovery sequence rather than loss of command or communication.

decisions.action: With safety and permission prerequisites confirmed, perform the authorized reset defined by the approved machine procedure and inspect the resulting drive state.
Issue repeated resets without confirming prerequisites or preserving the diagnostic state.

stages.title: Execute a controlled start
stages.situation: The authorized reset has completed and the drive is confirmed operationally ready for controlled movement.

decisions.action: Clear the hazardous area and execute an authorized controlled start while observing drive and machine response.
Release the conveyor to production as soon as the drive reports ready, without a controlled movement test.

stages.title: Validate recovery
stages.situation: The conveyor has moved during a controlled test, but production release still requires complete validation.

decisions.action: Validate controlled stop, authorized recovery, restart, safety behavior, and documentation before production handover.
End the intervention after observing one successful movement and record only that the conveyor restarted.

visual.educational_purpose: Show command intent, safety permission, drive readiness, and physical movement as distinct observable states during controlled recovery.
